title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes that continue the Longue Marche. The surrounding pages build, for a profinite group 𝔊 = 𝔊^+ ⋊ {1,τ}, an extension G_{ρ,σ} of a quotient group γ_{ρ,σ} by 𝔊^+. Here τ is an involution that plays the role of complex conjugation. The group 𝔊^+ is most likely a profinite modular-type group with distinguished elements ρ and σ (probably elliptic elements of orders 3 and 2, or 6 and 4) and ε_0, probably a cusp or loop generator. On the previous page, G_{ρ,σ} = So G_{ρ,σ}/Im L_0^♮, where So G_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔊^+ is a 'semi-direct' amalgam of a group of tuples Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut × Ẑ^* × μ × μ with 𝔊^+. It sits in a ladder of exact sequences (32) over γ_{ρ,σ}. Three characters are defined on G: χ_G (cyclotomic-type, values in Ẑ^*) and ε_{2G}, ε_{3G} (signs in μ = {±1}).

This page:
(36) τ_G and τ_γ are the images of τ_2. 𝔊 is identified with the inverse image of {1,τ_γ} ⊂ γ_{ρ,σ} in G_{ρ,σ}. 𝔊^♮ is the analogous inverse image in G^♮_{ρ,σ}.
(37) On 𝔊 the three characters coincide: χ_G|𝔊 = ε_{2G}|𝔊 = ε_{3G}|𝔊 =: ε_𝔊. This character is trivial on 𝔊^+ and equals -1 on τ, so on 𝔊 the cyclotomic character takes only the values ±1, as complex conjugation should.
(38) The canonical map Φ: G^♮_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} → Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ^* × μ × μ sends u to (int(u)|𝔊^+, χ_G(u), ε_{2G}(u), ε_{3G}(u)). It is well defined because 𝔊^+ is normal.

Proposition. Φ is a group homomorphism. Its image is the set of (u, λ, ε_2, ε_3) satisfying (39):
(a) u(ρ) is 𝔊^♮-conjugate to ε_3[τ]ρ, meaning ρ or its τ-twist according to the sign ε_3;
(b) likewise u(σ) is conjugate to ε_2[τ]σ;
(c) u(ε_0) is 𝔊^♮-conjugate to ε_0^λ, the inertia/cusp condition with cyclotomic exponent;
(d) u stabilises 𝔊^♮. This is automatic except in a case linked to (a), (b), namely when ε_2 = ε_3.
Its kernel (40) consists of the elements f^{-1}·u(f), with f ∈ 𝔊^♮ and u(f) = (int f, 1, 1, 1) ∈ Z^{0}_{ρ,σ}.

Corollary (41), finished on the next page. Put Z_0 = Cent_{𝔊^+}(L_0) and Z_0^♮ = Z_0 ∩ 𝔊^♮. Then L_0^♮ is a central subgroup of Z_0^♮, and f ↦ f^{-1}u(f) gives the exact sequence 1 → L_0^♮ → Z_0^♮ → G^♮_{ρ,σ} → G̃^♮_{ρ,σ} → 1, where G̃ is the set of tuples satisfying (39).

Purpose. This is a GT-type description, for an orbifold with elliptic points of orders 2 and 3 and one cusp (the M_{1,1} / SL_2(Z) situation), of a 'Teichmüller–Galois' group. It is characterised as automorphisms of 𝔊^+ that respect the conjugacy classes of the elliptic and cusp generators, twisted by signs and a cyclotomic exponent, up to a controlled kernel. The next page remarks that the extension construction is finer than simply defining the group as a subgroup of Aut(𝔊^+) with extra data (λ, ε, ε') added on.
errors: Inconsistent notation: Aut(𝔊^*) in the statement versus Aut(𝔊^+) in (38). This is a slip; it should be 𝔊^+.
The kernel description writes Z^{0+}_{ρ,σ}, while the corollary writes Z^0_{ρ,σ}. The intended group is ambiguous, though the difference is harmless since the characters are trivial.
Condition (d) is stated vaguely: 'automatic except ... a), b) if ε_2 = ε_3'. The exact exceptional case is not worked out on the page.
On the previous page ε_{3G} is written δ_G ε_{3γ} rather than ε_{3γ}∘δ_G. This is a notational slip.
The proof of the description of the image is not given; it is only asserted.

ideas.what: Group-theoretic GT-like group for the modular orbifold. It is realised as an extension of γ_{ρ,σ} by profinite 𝔊^+ and mapped to Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ^* × μ × μ. The image is cut out by conjugacy conditions on the elliptic generators (with sign twists ε_2, ε_3) and on the cusp generator (with cyclotomic exponent).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group for M_{1,1} / profinite SL_2(Z); automorphisms preserving inertia conjugacy classes ('Galois-type' or 'inertia-preserving' automorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (genus 1 and higher-genus Teichmüller tower GT); Enriquez (elliptic GT)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), which stresses the role of M_{1,1} and the elliptic points of orders 2 and 3. This explicit description is in unpublished notes.

ideas.what: Kernel of the map from an extension to Aut(normal subgroup) × characters, identified with Z_0^♮/L_0^♮ (centraliser modulo central subgroup) via f ↦ f^{-1}u(f). This yields a 4-term exact sequence.
ideas.modern_name: Standard extension theory (kernel of outer action / centraliser exact sequence)

ideas.what: Restriction of the cyclotomic character and of the two sign characters to the 'real' part 𝔊 = 𝔊^+ ⋊ {1,τ}: all three coincide, and τ acts as complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation in GT / extended (orientation-reversing) mapping class groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a precise structure theorem for a GT-type group attached to the modular orbifold with two elliptic points. Separate sign characters ε_2, ε_3 track the order-2 and order-3 elliptic generators, alongside the cyclotomic character, and the kernel is controlled by a centraliser. As far as I know, these sign refinements and the 'finer than Aut(𝔊^+)' extension construction are not in the published GT literature in this form.
missed.quote: u(ρ) est 𝔊^♮-conj. à ε_3[τ]ρ ; u(σ) ——— ε_2[τ]σ ; u(ε_0) est 𝔊^♮-conjugué à ε_0^μ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Genus-1 and orbifold versions of GT, such as elliptic GT, Γ_{1,1} and the work of Nakamura, Hoshi–Minamide and Lochak–Schneps, handle elliptic points and complex conjugation in varying ways. Grothendieck's explicit sign-character bookkeeping and his kernel computation could be compared with those treatments. Whether they give new information is unclear without the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, unpublished, technical construction of a GT-like group for the modular orbifold, with elliptic-point sign characters. It fits the known Esquisse programme and anticipates genus-1 GT work, but the page itself is mostly routine extension-theory bookkeeping. Its novelty is hard to judge without the definitions of ρ, σ, L_0 and Z_{ρ,σ}.
transcription_corrections: '𝔊^♮_t-conj.' is probably just '𝔊^♮-conj.' with a stray stroke.
In (36) the first line maps via G_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}. 'par 𝔊_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}' is a misreading of the struck-over symbol.
In the statement 'Aut(𝔊^*)' is Grothendieck's own slip for Aut(𝔊^+).
The header '633' is Grothendieck's own pagination; the archive page is 660.
